task.title: Line with the Largest Sum
task.statement:
Create a file solution.py containing the function:

def max_sum_line(text):

text is a multi-line string. Each line holds integers separated by whitespace. Find the line whose numbers add up to the largest sum and return the tuple (line_index, line_sum), where line_index is the 0-based index of that line.

Example:
    max_sum_line("1 2 3\n10 20\n4 4 4")  ->  (1, 30)
task.notes:
Planted ambiguities — resolve ONLY if asked, one short sentence each:
1. How should blank or whitespace-only lines be treated? -> They count as real lines with sum 0 and keep their position in the line numbering.
2. If two lines tie for the largest sum, which one do I return? -> Return the earliest such line (the one with the smallest index).
3. Does a trailing newline at the end of the input create an extra empty line? -> No — a single trailing newline does not add a line (splitlines-style line splitting).
If asked anything not listed here: the statement is all they get.
task.appendix:
Designed to elicit: str.splitlines + a list comprehension with sum(map(int, line.split())) for per-line sums, then max(enumerate(...), key=...) to get (index, sum) in one expression; relies on max returning the first maximal element for tie-breaking.

Watch for: Java-shaped version: text.split("\n"), a manual counter variable i incremented in a for loop (or range(len(lines))), an inner for loop over line.split() accumulating s += int(tok), and best_sum/best_idx variables updated with if s > best_sum — plus a bug where blank lines are skipped with continue (shifting indices) or where a trailing newline manufactures a phantom (n, 0) line.

Hidden checks (for after the session — the interviewer never runs these):
assert max_sum_line("1 2 3\n10 20\n4 4 4") == (1, 30)
assert max_sum_line("2 3\n5\n1 1") == (0, 5)
assert max_sum_line("1 2\n\n3 9") == (2, 12)
assert max_sum_line("-5 -1\n\n-2") == (1, 0)
assert max_sum_line("-1 -2\n-3 -1\n") == (0, -3)
assert max_sum_line("1\n   \n2") == (2, 2)
assert max_sum_line("7") == (0, 7)

Reference:
def max_sum_line(text):
    line_sums = [sum(map(int, line.split())) for line in text.splitlines()]
    return max(enumerate(line_sums), key=lambda pair: pair[1])
